builds.name: PPC pacing and performance assistant
builds.vision: Pacing and proactive performance alerts for every PPC account. Account managers only open an account when something is flagged: either it needs a change, or there's a winning ad worth doubling down on. The alerts are connected to the client brain, so the AI isn't reviewing the ad account in isolation. It looks at the same data and context a manager would use to triage and make an educated decision – the client's goals, history, recent conversations and what's been tried before, their industry, competitor intel, seasonality and market trends. Later, the same system can take autonomous action within the limits the team sets.
vision_bullets: Daily pacing across every live channel, flagged when a client is off pace.
Proactive performance alerts on each client's own KPIs and thresholds – problems to fix and winners to scale.
Every alert comes with a diagnosis drawn from the account data and the client brain – the same context a manager would use.
Later: autonomous action within agreed limits (e.g. moving budget to a winning ad, pausing a failing one), with the manager kept informed.
problems: Budgets are kept by hand in three places and some channels, including LinkedIn, aren't tracked; one missed budget change cost a $10,000 credit – critical; raised by 3 staff and leadership.
The Meta pacing sheet is broken because the Supermetrics feed keeps failing – critical; raised by 3 staff.
There's no performance alerting, so problems are found at month-end – the widest raise in paid media, 7 staff.
When performance drops, working out why means jumping between platforms and the client's history – the diagnosis part of the alerting problem raised by 7 staff.
The weekly account check is done by hand, account by account, and clients often hear about results only at month-end.
how: Windsor.ai (bought, data only)

pulls spend and performance from every channel Aperitif runs – Google, Meta, Microsoft, LinkedIn, TikTok, Pinterest, Reddit, ChatGPT ads, Criteo and DV360 – into one place each day, and exposes it to the AI through its MCP connection and API.
Pacing engine (Transpera build)

a budget register holds each client's monthly budget per channel and every change, dated. A daily job compares spend to date with where it should be (straight-line or a set flight plan), forecasts month-end, and flags anything outside the agreed range.
Performance alerts (Transpera build)
each client's KPIs and thresholds (CPA, ROAS, conversions, CTR) are checked daily against target and the last 4–8 weeks; drops, spikes, stopped spend and clear winners are flagged.
Performance assistant (Transpera build)

every flag goes to Slack tagging the account owner, and an AI agent reads the account through Windsor alongside the client brain (goals, history, recent conversations, what's been tried, industry, competitor intel, seasonality and market trends) and posts a diagnosis and a recommended next step in the thread.
Later phase
autonomous actions through Windsor's write actions (Google and Meta budgets, pausing), within limits agreed per client, every change logged and the manager notified.
future: Budgets are entered once, with every change logged and dated.
Spend from every live channel is pulled automatically each day; nobody fills a sheet.
Account managers open an account only when it's flagged – to fix something or to double down on a winner.
Every alert comes with a diagnosis and a recommended next step, so the manager starts deciding rather than investigating.
Winning ads and audiences are spotted early and scaled, not found at month-end.
No spend goes live on a channel without a pacing line.

builds.name: Client brain
builds.vision: The connective tissue of the business. One AI brain that links every piece of software, document, client conversation and process into one view of the business – and inside it, a smaller brain for every client. Each client brain holds everything about that client: their goals and KPIs, contacts, contract and services, call transcripts, emails and Slack threads, Monday tasks and deliverables, ad and analytics performance, decisions made and what's been tried before, assets and artefacts. Leadership can ask where anything is at from a single chat bar and get an answer with sources, across every client or for one. Staff never miss a beat: open a client brain and the full story is there, and the brain calls out what matters before anyone asks. It is also the shared memory every other system we build plugs into. Because the PPC assistant, brief drafts, client comms, onboarding audit and client health tools all read from and write back to the same brain, they behave as intelligent agents rather than automations: they know the client's goals, history and what's been tried, reason about what to do next, and get smarter as the team's feedback and every result are saved back.
vision_bullets: One business brain, many client brains: every client has its own brain inside the company brain, so answers about a client only draw on that client's information – and leadership can still ask across all of them.
What's in each client brain: goals and KPIs, contacts, contract and services, calls, emails, Slack, Monday tasks, deliverables, ad and analytics performance, decisions and what's been tried, assets.
Connective tissue: links Slack, email, Otter calls, Monday, HubSpot, Drive, Notion and the ad accounts automatically – nobody copies information in.
One chat bar for leadership: "where is this at?", "which clients are at risk?", "what did we promise them?" – answered with sources.
Staff never miss a beat: client history, open actions and how-we-do-it processes are always one question away, and handovers come with the brain attached.
Proactive: surfaces key facts, risks and missed actions for each client without being asked.

Shared memory for every agent: each system we build reads the client brain before it acts and writes back what it did and what happened – so they're intelligent agents that reason with full context, not automations following fixed rules.
Gets smarter over time: the team's feedback, approved and rejected recommendations, and results are stored, so every agent learns what works for each client.
problems: Client knowledge lives in people's heads and personal docs, not in one place per client – high; raised by 4 staff.
Preparing for a client call can take longer than the call – high; raised by 4 staff.
Handovers – sales to delivery, cover, offboarding – have no structured pack or trigger – high; raised by 3 staff.
how: Business brain
shared knowledge – SOPs and processes (Notion), team, services, pricing, templates – plus a cross-client view for leadership questions.
Client brains

one per client, built from a standard record (goals, KPIs, contacts, services, budgets, key dates) and filled automatically by connectors – Otter transcripts, Gmail, Slack client channels, HubSpot, Monday, Windsor (performance) and Drive/Notion docs. Every item is tagged to its client so answers stay within that client.
Each new call is summarised with actions into the client brain within 24 hours; a weekly digest per client flags changes, risks and open actions.
The team asks questions in Slack (one chat bar) and gets answers with sources, plus a prep pack before every meeting; access follows who works on the client, with leadership seeing all.
Agent layer

every other build connects to the brain through one shared interface – it reads the client brain for context before acting (goals, history, past decisions, what's been tried) and writes back its output, the manager's feedback and the result. One memory, many agents.
future: Every active client has one brain; nothing about the client lives only in someone's head or personal doc.

Every client call is recorded; its transcript, summary, key call-outs and actions are saved to the client's page within 24 hours. Key client emails are saved the same way. Anyone can read them without querying.
Before a call, the manager asks for a brief and gets the last call's actions, open items and month-on-month performance in one view.
When a client changes hands or offboards, a handover report is generated in under three clicks.
Anyone working on the client – SEO, paid, content, writers – queries the same brain instead of asking a colleague.
Every agent Transpera builds works from the same client context, so recommendations get more specific to each client over time instead of repeating generic rules.

builds.name: Link-building system
builds.vision: One AI-native system that runs the whole link-building operation. Orders, publishers, live links and invoices live in one place with one ID; domains are pre-vetted and matched to clients; every paid link is watched after it goes live; and unlinked brand mentions are turned into free links. The link lead spends their time growing supply and the team, not keeping spreadsheets in sync. Every link built feeds the client brain, so anyone can see which links a client has, where, and whether they're still live.
vision_bullets: One system, one ID: orders, publishers, live links and payments tracked once; publishers update their own orders through a portal.
Supply engine: one shared vetting skill checks domains for quality and spam and matches them to clients – the link lead only reviews a shortlist.
Link watchdog: every live paid link is checked on a schedule; missing or changed links alert the team with a refund or replacement email drafted.
Brand mentions: unlinked mentions of Tier 1 and 2 clients are found, ranked and drafted as outreach.
Connected to the client brain: each client's link history, live status and spend sit in their brain and flow into reporting.
problems: Link building runs on seven or more disconnected spreadsheets, with about 2,830 orders this year – raised by staff and leadership.
Outreacher invoices are tracked as PayPal links in spreadsheet cells, and the link lead's time goes on admin rather than links.
Home-built link tools are understood by only one person.

builds.name: Brief drafts
builds.vision: The month's content work comes straight out of the plan that already exists. The content team fills in a short standard form for the details that need to be consistent; the AI combines it with the content plan in the client's Master SEO Document and drafts every brief in Aperitif's template. Once the SEO manager approves a brief, it becomes a Monday task for the right writer with a due date. Nobody re-cuts the plan, retypes it into tasks or chases whether a brief was seen. Over time, the brief also draws on the client brain – tone, compliance and what's worked before – so drafts need fewer edits.

The team points it at the new client's site and accounts, and it runs the audit and fills in the onboarding documents – the Master SEO Document for SEO clients and the 30-point paid audit checklist for paid clients. It flags what needs attention and drafts first recommendations; the strategist reviews, adds the strategy and signs off. A new client's audit is ready within a day of access, not spread across most of month one.

builds.name: Sales handover
builds.vision: A won deal creates the new client's record in the client brain, already filled in. The handover pulls together everything sales learned – the sales meeting transcripts, the HubSpot deal (notes, emails, contacts, quote and services sold), the signed proposal and any forms or documents the client shared – and extracts the goals, promises, budgets, timelines, key people and risks. The sales rep only answers a short set of questions for what's missing, and each delivery department confirms or questions the handover before kick-off. Nobody goes into a first client call blind, and the client is never asked again what they already told sales.
vision_bullets: Triggered by HubSpot: a deal marked won starts the handover with no manual step.
Extracts from every sales source: meeting transcripts, HubSpot deal notes, emails and contacts, the quote and services sold, the signed proposal and shared documents.
Pulls out what delivery needs: goals, KPIs, promises made, budgets, timelines, key contacts, prerequisites and risks – each point linked to its source.
The rep only fills gaps through a short question set.
Each department confirms it can deliver, or flags why not, before kick-off; denied deals and reasons are logged for sales.
Lives in the client brain for the life of the client – what was sold and promised is always one question away.

Clients are sometimes sold without delivery prerequisites in place, such as a working website.

It extracts goals, KPIs, promises, budgets, timelines, key contacts, prerequisites and risks into the standard handover template, each point linked to its source, and flags what's missing.
The sales rep answers a short question set for the gaps; the handover is saved to the client brain and each delivery department confirms or questions it before kick-off.

Missing prerequisites (such as a working website) are flagged before kick-off, not discovered in month one.

builds.name: Client Retention and Growth AI
builds.vision: An anti-churn and growth engine that is present in every meeting, email and deliverable. It doesn't just scan for keywords and phrases – it reads behaviour and patterns across the whole relationship, the way an experienced account director would. It notices when meetings start getting cancelled or pushed, when replies slow down, when the senior contact stops turning up, when a new stakeholder appears, when approvals and invoices drag, when sentiment cools across calls, emails and Slack, and when results drift away from the client's goals. It also spots growth: new goals, strong results worth building on, and services the client doesn't have yet. Running on the client brain, it builds a picture of each person at the client – how they communicate, what they care about and how their sentiment is trending – and when something shows, it alerts the account manager, department lead and Head of Client Services together, with the evidence and a suggested next step. Every outcome is logged, so it learns which signals really matter for Aperitif's clients.
vision_bullets: Behaviour, not keywords: tracks patterns over time – meetings cancelled, rescheduled or no-showed, slower response times, fewer people on calls, a senior contact going quiet, new stakeholders appearing, delayed approvals, late payments, requests to cut scope or budget, and requests for data exports or account access.
Sentiment across all comms: tone tracked per person across calls, emails and Slack, so a cooling relationship shows up as a trend, not a single bad email.
Results against goals: performance drifting away from what the client cares about, before they raise it.
Growth signals: new goals, strong results that justify a bigger budget, and services that fit but aren't sold yet (e.g. an SEO client with no paid media) – fed into call prep, reviews and proposals.
Live retention and growth scores for every client, with leadership seeing portfolio health in one view.
Alerts with evidence and a next step, well before a client leaves; people own the escalation.
